Internet and ERP both unavailable at the same site

WAN edge interface or optic failure

required_evidence.description: Core-side termination is alive

steps.expected_observation: Line protocol down with carrier loss

steps.action: Check routing adjacency over the WAN link

commands.purpose: BGP session state and prefixes received

steps.expected_observation: BGP or OSPF neighbor down after the interface failure

steps.action: Confirm the core-side device is still reporting telemetry

playbooks.title: Packet loss and degradation on a WAN circuit
playbooks.description: Users at a branch report slowness and choppy calls while the WAN circuit stays up but drops packets.
symptoms: Slow application response at one branch
possible_causes: Physical degradation on the carrier circuit
Faulty optic, cable or interface
Congestion on an undersized circuit

required_evidence.description: Packet loss above threshold on the WAN interface

decisions.condition: Loss coincides with rising errors and normal utilization
decisions.conclusion: Treat as physical or circuit degradation

decisions.condition: Loss coincides with utilization above 90 percent
decisions.conclusion: Treat as congestion and review capacity

decisions.condition: Loss measured only while the interface is down

escalation.condition: Sustained loss above 5 percent for more than 10 minutes

playbooks.title: OSPF adjacency failure with links up
playbooks.description: A site loses routes because an OSPF adjacency is stuck or down even though the physical link reports up.
symptoms: Site cannot reach data centre applications while the WAN circuit shows up
Routes to a site disappear from the core
Recent configuration change on a WAN edge router
possible_causes: Interface MTU mismatch between neighbors
Area, network type or timer mismatch
Authentication mismatch after a configuration change

required_evidence.description: Adjacency not FULL while both interfaces are up
Routes withdrawn at the time of the adjacency change
Configuration or MTU change shortly before the failure

steps.action: Analyze routing adjacencies on the site WAN edge

commands.purpose: OSPF neighbor list and adjacency state

steps.expected_observation: Adjacency stuck in EXSTART or similar with links up

escalation.condition: Routes withdrawn for a whole site

playbooks.title: Application traffic blocked by firewall policy
playbooks.description: One application fails for a site while the routed path stays healthy, because a firewall rule denies the traffic.
symptoms: One application portal times out for a single site

possible_causes: New or reordered deny rule matching the traffic
Overly broad source or destination object
Rule shadowing after a policy commit

required_evidence.description: Flows to the application denied by a specific rule

commands.purpose: Recently denied traffic and matching rules

decisions.condition: Denies by a recently modified rule and a reachable path

escalation.condition: Business application denied for a whole site

documents.title: Evidence principles for network diagnosis
documents.content: Diagnostic tool evidence is authoritative; playbooks are guidance only. Missing telemetry is not proof of failure. Confirm a fault with at least two independent observations before escalating, record contradicting evidence, and consider shared upstream devices when several sites fail together. All recommended commands are read-only.

documents.title: Illustrative read-only command reference
documents.content: Commands in this knowledge base are illustrative read-only examples for Cisco IOS XE style routers and switches (show, ping, traceroute), PAN-OS style firewalls (show) and Linux servers (journalctl, dig, rndc status, keactrl status). Placeholders in braces must be filled in by the engineer. Configuration commands are never recommended.

documents.title: Escalation matrix by fault domain
documents.content: WAN and carrier faults: WAN Operations / carrier liaison. Routing faults: Network Engineering - Routing. Firewall policy: Network Security Operations. 802.1X and RADIUS: Network Access Control team. DHCP and DNS: Infrastructure Services - DHCP/DNS. Shared core or data centre devices: Network Operations - Core and Data Centre. Unknown domain: Network Operations - L2 triage. Escalations are recommendations until a person sends them.
